columns.name: count

assumptions: The rate changes smoothly from one cell to the cells near it
The map changes only from one era (a group of periods) to the next
The total for the full grid changes gradually from one period to the next
Events can occur in groups (more variation than a constant rate gives)
avoid_when: You have exact locations and want a model for each point (bin them into cells first)
The grid has thousands of cells (the fit becomes too slow)
You must know what occurs if a cause changes, such as a new policy (the model has no columns for causes)
You need a forecast further ahead than the model permits without a new fit
data_needs: A count of events for each cell and each period (quarters, months or years)
Cells of equal size, with the row and column number of each cell
about.example: Count the earthquakes in each 25 km cell for each quarter from 2009 to 2017. Then forecast the map and the total for 2018 and 2019 with a 90% range.
about.expert_notes: Log-Gaussian Cox process on a space-time grid (pymc-challenges E07, rung 4). log rate = alpha + g_t + log softmax over cells of f_era(s): the total per period (exp(alpha + g_t), g a centred Gaussian random walk) is separate from the share of each cell, so the field cannot inflate the total. f is a 2-D Hilbert-space GP (Matern-5/2, product basis of m_row x m_col sine functions, boundary factor c) whose basis coefficients follow a random walk over eras, anchored at the busiest fit era. Negative binomial counts (prior on 1/phi). The random-walk steps and the era coefficients cover max_extension periods after the fit, so forecasts use posterior draws of their prior. Lengthscale prior: inverse gamma with 90% of its mass between ell_lower_km and ell_upper_km.
outputs: The expected events for each cell and period, with a range
The expected total for each period, with a range
Forecasts of the map and of the total for the next periods

references.title: Moller, Syversveen and Waagepetersen (1998), Log Gaussian Cox processes
Riutort-Mayol et al. (2022), Practical Hilbert space approximate Bayesian Gaussian processes

about.summary_plain: Finds where and when events such as earthquakes occur more often. It counts the events in each cell of a map for each period, and it forecasts the next periods with a range.
about.title: Event counts on a map over time
use_when: You have counts of events in each cell of a regular grid for each period
The area with many events moves or changes over time
You want a map of the expected rate and a map of the uncertainty

manifest.description: A log-Gaussian Cox process for event counts on a regular space-time grid: a random-walk total per period times a smooth 2-D map (Matérn-5/2 HSGP) that can change from era to era, with negative-binomial counts. Forecasts reach at most max_extension periods past the fit.

rate.description: Events per cell and period: the expected intensity, or a predictive count draw

total.description: Expected events per period in the whole grid

alpha_sigma.description: Sd of the log total per period (centred on the fit mean)
alpha_sigma.title: Alpha Sigma

anchor.description: The era whose map gets the marginal prior; the other eras walk away from it (busiest = the fit era with the most events)
anchor.title: Anchor

cell_km.description: Width of one grid cell in km
cell_km.title: Cell Km

era_periods.description: Periods in one era: the spatial field changes from era to era (4 quarters = one map per year)
era_periods.title: Era Periods

eta0_scale.description: Half-normal scale of the anchor map
eta0_scale.title: Eta0 Scale

eta_d_scale.description: Half-normal scale of the era increments
eta_d_scale.title: Eta D Scale

field.description: era_walk: a new map each era (a random walk of maps); static: one map for all periods (the separable model)
field.title: Field

max_extension.description: Periods a forecast may reach past the fitted range without a refit (x-ui-level: basic)
max_extension.title: Max Extension

sigma_g_scale.description: Half-normal scale of the RW step
sigma_g_scale.title: Sigma G Scale
